subject: Liability exposure allocation — proposal and redlines
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MSA — liability cap and carve-outs

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal has a couple of open items on the MSA we wanted to get aligned on before procurement moves to a PO. The primary ask is around the liability cap — our standard is either (i) aggregate cap equal to fees paid under the contract or (ii) 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months.

We also need explicit carve-outs for IP infringement, willful misconduct, and data protection regulatory fines, but we want to preserve consequential damages carve-outs only in limited circumstances (e.g., loss of business if Redwood is grossly negligent).

I attached our redline for reference (Acme_MSA_Redlines_20260720.docx). Can you let me know whether Redwood can accept an annualized multiple (3x prior 12 months) or if you require the cap to be aggregate for the whole term?

Appreciate a short call if that's easier.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Contracts, Acme Corp

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — liability cap and carve-outs

Sara —

Thanks for the redline and clear framing. High level: Redwood typically offers two patterns depending on commercial scale and risk profile:

- Option A (recommended for self-serve/smaller deals): cap = greater of $X (we'll propose a floor) or 2x fees paid in prior 12 months (annualized multiple).
- Option B (enterprise / enterprise SLAs): cap = 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months, with narrow carve-outs for IP, gross negligence, and regulatory fines.

We generally resist an aggregate cap tied to total fees for the full term because that can under-index for long-term/expanding usage. Annualization gives both parties predictable exposure each year.

I'll route this to legal for firm language and a redline. Can you confirm whether Acme needs a per-incident threshold (e.g., $250k) in addition to the aggregate/annual cap, or is the multiple sufficient?

Happy to hop on 30 min tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0112

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood MSA — liability cap and carve-outs (legal proposed language)

Vanessa / Laura / Kim —

Quick legal take and recommended redline attached (RW_proposed_cap_language_20260721_redline.docx). Key points we should propose back to Acme: 

1) Use an annualized cap calculated as the greater of: (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months * 2.5 OR (b) a negotiated floor (we suggest $100k for this tier). The multiplier is negotiable — suggest start at 2.5 to land at 3 with concessions.
2) Carve-outs we will accept: (i) IP infringement resulting in third-party claims; (ii) damages arising from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence; (iii) statutory regulatory fines and penalties.
3) Exclude consequential and special damages except to the extent arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. That language narrows Acme's broad ask while keeping standard protections.
4) No unlimited liability for data breaches — instead include explicit indemnity for data breaches caused by Redwood subject to the cap (we typically accept carve-outs only for third-party claims and regulatory fines).

Attach includes precise redline suggestions and a short rationale paragraph we can paste into the reply email.

If Acme insists on aggregate-term 3x fees, advise asking procurement for a higher commercial commitment (longer term or minimum annual commit) in exchange.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — liability cap and carve-outs

Sara —

Appreciate the patience. Legal reviewed and we have a concrete proposal attached (RW_proposed_cap_language_20260721_redline.docx). Summary of what we suggest for Acme to review:

• Cap structure: annualized cap = greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months * 2.5, or (ii) $100,000 floor. We are willing to consider 3x the prior 12 months for an approved enterprise order form.

• Carve-outs: explicit carve-outs for third-party IP infringement claims, Redwood gross negligence/willful misconduct, and regulatory fines.

• Consequential damages: excluded except for those caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

• Data incidents: we will accept contractual responsibility for data incidents caused by Redwood, but remediation/penalties are subject to the cap (regulatory fines carve-out remains).

If Acme's priority is a single-term aggregate cap at 3x total fees, our counter would be to ask for a 24–36 month committed spend or a minimum annual commitment.

Next steps: please confirm whether Acme can live with annualized language or if you need an aggregate-term formulation. If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute legal-to-legal call tomorrow afternoon — Aditya can join.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — liability cap and carve-outs

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear options and for routing legal language. We reviewed internally. Acme's position: we can accept an annualized approach for deals where our spend profile is stable year-to-year, but for our initial deployment we prefer a single-term aggregate cap of 2x total fees for the first 12 months with a view to move to an annual reset on renewal.

On carve-outs: we can live with IP and willful misconduct carve-outs. We need consequential damages to remain broadly excluded (including lost profits) except expressly where Redwood is grossly negligent. Also please expand the data incident language so it explicitly excludes statutory regulatory fines from cap (we appreciate your note that you expect those excluded, but want explicit language).

I've attached our annotated counter-redline (Acme_MSA_Redlines_20260720.docx) with line notes that mirror what I wrote above. If you can send a 1-page summary of the proposed trade (annualized cap vs aggregate + commercial commitment) for procurement, that will help us close quickly.

Can we target a procurement decision by EOD next Wednesday?

Regards,
Sara
